ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The diagram shows the front and right-hand views of a solid made up of cubes of side $3\mathrm{~cm}$. The maximum volume that the solid could have is $V\mathrm{~cm}^{3}$. What is the value of $V$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left-side view in the figure is composed of 4 columns of squares, and the heights of the columns from left to right are 2, 1, 2, 1. The right-side view also has 4 positions, and the heights of the positions from left to right are 1, 2, 2, 1. The problem states that these are the front view and right view of a solid composed of small cubes with side length 3 cm. Reasoning: Regard the solid as a 4×4 base grid, and several unit cubes can be placed on each cell. The stacking height at a certain position cannot exceed the corresponding front-view column height, and also cannot exceed the corresponding right-view depth height, so the maximum height is the smaller value of these two restrictions. Let the front-view heights be [2,1,2,1], and the right-view heights be [1,2,2,1]. Take min cell by cell and sum: when the front-view height is 2, comparing with the right view gives 1+2+2+1=6; when the front-view height is 1, it gives 1+1+1+1=4; the total number for the four columns is 6+4+6+4=20 small cubes. The volume of each small cube is 3^3=27 cm^3, so the maximum volume V=20×27=540 cm^3.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram shows the front and right-hand views of a solid made up of cubes of side $3\mathrm{~cm}$. The maximum volume that the solid could have is $V\mathrm{~cm}^{3}$. What is the value of $V$?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the left/front view is 4 columns wide with heights 2, 1, 2, 1, and the right-hand view is 4 positions deep with heights 1, 2, 2, 1. Model the solid as a 4-by-4 grid of vertical stacks of unit cubes. For each grid position, the stack height cannot exceed both its front-view column height and its right-view depth height, so the maximum possible stack height is the minimum of those two values. Sum all 16 values min(front height, right height) to get the maximum number of cubes, then multiply by the volume of one cube, 3^3 cm^3.

推理：把立体看成一个4×4的底面网格，每个格子上可以放若干个单位立方体。某个位置的堆叠高度不能超过对应正视图列高度，也不能超过对应右视图深度高度，所以最大高度为这两个限制的较小值。设正视图高度为[2,1,2,1]，右视图高度为[1,2,2,1]。逐格取min并求和：当正视图高度为2时，与右视图比较得到1+2+2+1=6；当正视图高度为1时，得到1+1+1+1=4；四列总数为6+4+6+4=20个小立方体。每个小立方体体积为3^3=27 cm^3，所以最大体积V=20×27=540 cm^3。

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram in layers: both views show 4 occupied positions along their bottom row, while the front view has second-level squares only above columns 1 and 3, and the right-hand view has second-level squares only above the middle two depth positions. Count cubes by horizontal layers. On level 1, every front column and every depth position is allowed, so the maximum footprint has 4×4 cubes. On level 2, only 2 front columns and 2 depth positions can contain cubes, so the maximum second layer has 2×2 cubes. There is no third layer. Add the layer counts and multiply by 27 cm^3 per cube.

推理：按水平层数计算最多立方体数。第1层中，前视图允许4个横向位置，右视图允许4个深度位置，所以最多可放4×4=16个小立方体。第2层中，前视图只允许第1、3列有方块，右视图只允许第2、3个深度位置有方块，所以最多可放2×2=4个小立方体。总小立方体数为16+4=20。每个小立方体边长为3 cm，体积为3^3=27 cm^3。因此最大体积V=20×27=540 cm^3。
